decisions.executionNote: Begin right-arm elbow-up approach to the key; key is farther forward than the reference. Keep left parked and grippers open.
Continue smooth elbow-up rotation and forward approach; stay above the key before lowering.
Move right wrist toward a downward grasp over the shaft, using modest increments to preserve joint continuity.
Finish downward approach over the key shaft; inspect wrist alignment before closing.
Fine-align the right gripper near the base of the shaft, matching the key's slight yaw before grasping.
Use wrist-image servoing to bring the shaft base into the pinch zone; retain open jaws during this small forward correction.
Center the shaft between the right fingertips, then close fully. Retention will be checked visually during a short lift.
Allow the right fingers to finish closing, then make a short vertical test lift while keeping the grasp closed.
Lift the key clear of the table with a closed right grasp; check that the key follows rather than slipping.
Key follows the lift but has pivoted in the pinch. Raise it for clearance and stage a visually adjusted handover instead of assuming the reference grasp.
The key slipped and is visible on the table. Reopen and approach the bow/shaft junction in its new horizontal orientation for a more secure grasp.
Align downward fingers across the new key direction and descend over the shaft close to the bow, leaving table clearance.
Translate the key into the wrist-view pinch corridor, accounting for link6-to-fingertip offset; lower gently with the jaws open.
Fine-center the shaft in the open jaws and reach grasp height; the key is now viewed edge-on, so closing must be slow and checked.
Close progressively on the shaft near the bow while holding the wrist still, then verify retention with a gentle lift.
Finish closing without wrist motion, then test a one-centimeter lift to see whether the shaft stays captured.
The key now stays between the fingertips. Lift and move toward the central handover area, preserving its edge-on orientation.
Finish raising the retained key at the handover station while beginning the left arm's elbow-up approach.
Keep the right grasp stationary and bring the left wrist up and inward along the elbow-up approach.
Advance the receiving arm toward the central key while preserving elbow-up continuity; right hand remains closed and still.
Adjust the receiving jaw orientation for the key's vertical face rather than copying the flat-key handover; approach slowly with both arms separated.
Continue the receiving-hand approach with jaws oriented to pinch the edge-on bow. Keep the retained key stationary.
Bring the receiving fingertips level with the exposed key bow and finish aligning the side pinch, leaving a small approach gap.
Close the approach gap toward the bow without releasing the right grasp. Use the receiving wrist image to refine height and centering.
Advance the left fingertips around the exposed bow and partly narrow the opening; the right hand continues supporting the shaft.
Center the bow in the receiving pinch and close the left gripper fully while the right still supports the key.
Transfer support to the closed left gripper by gradually opening the right hand without moving either wrist.
Withdraw the open right hand to its own side while keeping the left bow grasp fixed; verify the key remains with the receiving hand.
The key slipped during transfer and is visible on the table. Clear the left hand to expose it before a right-hand recovery grasp.
Recover from above with the right hand, rotating the open jaws to the key's new direction. Move the left hand farther clear.
Continue the overhead recovery approach with the key now clearly visible; align to the shaft without crossing the centerline.
Align the recovered flat key with the right pinch corridor, stopping above the table and keeping the wrist on its own side.
Fine-align from the wrist image: center the lower shaft, correct yaw, and gently reach grasp height without crossing the wrists.
The key shifted during approach. Back the open pinch toward the bow and slightly raise for clearance before closing.
Translate without further rotation to center the shaft in the pinch corridor and avoid sweeping the key sideways.
The open fingertips are nudging the key. Lift clear before recentering so the next approach does not push it along the table.
With the jaws clear of the table, recenter over the key's current shaft and match its yaw before a straight descent.
Increase fingertip clearance first, then make the remaining centering correction above the key to avoid further contact.
Use a small isolated lateral correction at safe height to resolve wrist-image alignment before descending again.
Approach vertically from clearance, aligning over the shaft using the head view and checking the wrist perspective as height decreases.
Lift the open right gripper well clear to remove any residual contact, then reassess the key before another straight approach.
Replan after the continuity interruption with smaller steps, using the head view to place the wrist above the visible shaft.
Descend straight with yaw fixed and the jaws open, checking that the shaft enters the pinch area without lateral pushing.
Make a small jaw-lateral correction with slight clearance, checking its image effect before closing.
Correct the measured lateral direction and raise slightly, moving the open pinch back toward the key center.
Continue the verified lateral correction while staying on the right side, then begin narrowing around the bow.
Hold both wrists fixed and finish closing the right gripper; inspect the actual fingertips relative to the bow before lifting.
The closed fingertips missed the bow. Reopen and use a small wrist tilt to reach it without moving the right wrist across the centerline.
The key is now at the left side of center. Clear the right arm and prepare an overhead left-hand recovery while maintaining separated elbow-up configurations.
The prior chunk was rejected without motion. Use substantially smaller increments for both arms to preserve the current IK branch.
Continue clearing the right arm and gradually pitch the left wrist toward an overhead pickup, using small continuous joint changes.
The key is now clearly in the left workspace. Approach it from above with the left arm while withdrawing the right arm clear.
Replan the rejected motion at less than half the rotational increment to preserve the left wrist's current IK branch.
Continue a gradual elbow-up overhead approach with the left wrist, keeping the right arm moving away from the key.
Rotate the left fingers toward a downward pinch while staying above the key; finish parking the right hand outside the work area.
Finish bringing the left gripper above the shaft with a nearly downward approach; right hand remains clear and stationary.
Complete the downward orientation and lower toward the bow/shaft junction, keeping the open fingers above the table.
Apply a lateral correction with the downward wrist held fixed, bringing the key into the left pinch corridor before descending.
Lift the left fingers clear before adjusting yaw; the head view shows the key lies across the current jaw direction.
Align over the exposed shaft at clearance height, using the head view for position and keeping the other arm parked.
Bring the visible shaft toward the left pinch center and descend partway, matching its current yaw before closing.
Correct the large lateral wrist-image error with yaw fixed, keeping the left wrist in its own workspace.
Use the head-view fingertip alignment for a straight descent, then close at the shaft near the bow without further lateral sweeping.
